full_text:
Be realistic about what will cope with our summer sun.
SHARE
By Isaac Olson, Nursery Near Me
A plant in the ground has cool soil around its roots.
A plant in a pot can have a few centimetres of potting mix and a wall that sits in the sun all afternoon.
That is why pots are the first thing to suffer in a South East Queensland summer, and why an hour spent on them now saves a lot of plants in January.
- Advertisement -
Start with where they sit. Morning sun and afternoon shade suits most potted plants, so move what you can to the eastern side of the house or under a tree.
Group the pots together, because a cluster shades itself and holds a little humidity. Lift them off hot pavers and concrete with pot feet or a couple of bricks, which also lets them drain after a storm.
Next, look at the pots themselves. Small pots dry out in hours, and black plastic gets hot enough to cook the roots on the sunny side.
If a plant has filled its pot and the water runs straight through, move it up a size into fresh premium potting mix. Light coloured and thick walled pots stay cooler. A plain plastic pot slipped inside a larger decorative one is cooler again.
Then change how you water. Water early in the morning and keep going until it runs out of the bottom.
If the mix has shrunk away from the sides, sit the whole pot in a tub of water for half an hour so it wets right through. A layer of mulch on top of the mix slows the drying.
Saucers are handy in a heatwave, but empty them in wet weather so the roots do not sit in water and the mosquitoes do not breed.
Finally, be realistic about what will cope. Bougainvillea, frangipani, succulents, dwarf bottlebrush, lomandra and citrus all handle a hot pot in full sun. Ferns, hydrangeas and most indoor plants want shade and more water.
– Isaac Olson is a director of Nursery Near Me, an Australian online nursery that delivers to Ipswich, Logan and the Redlands, at nurserynearme.com.au.

full_text:
A powerful storm system continued to batter much of Greece on Saturday, with civil protection authorities placing the Ionian Islands, Epirus and western Greece under red code alert.
Serious flooding, landslides and power outages have already been reported, while further deterioration is forecast from Sunday, bringing northerly winds reaching 10 on the Beaufort scale in parts of the Aegean, a sharp drop in temperatures and snowfall in mountainous areas.
The severe weather is gradually spreading across much of the country. According to the National Meteorological Service (EMY) and data from Meteo.gr, heavy rain and thunderstorms are affecting western and northern mainland Greece, the Ionian Sea and the northeastern Aegean. From Saturday evening, conditions are expected to worsen in central Macedonia, particularly Pieria and Halkidiki, as well as eastern Thessaly. An orange warning is also in force for the western Peloponnese.
Heavy rain and thunderstorms caused flooding in Sivota, Thesprotia, as severe weather swept the region. (APOHXOS.GR / EUROKINISSI)
Further deterioration is forecast for Sunday, with heavy rain and thunderstorms initially affecting Thessaly, eastern central Greece — particularly Fthiotida prefecture — and Evia, before spreading to eastern and southern parts of the Peloponnese.
Northerly to northeasterly winds are expected to reach nine Beaufort in eastern areas and locally 10 Beaufort in the Aegean. Heavy snowfall is forecast in mountainous mainland areas, as well as in Florina.
When will the greater Athens area be affected?
In Attica prefecture, rain and isolated thunderstorms are expected from Saturday afternoon, with southerly winds of three to four Beaufort and temperatures ranging from 12 to 20 degrees Celsius.
On Sunday, temperatures are expected to drop considerably, with the first snowfall of the season forecast on Mount Parnitha. By Monday, the maximum temperature in Athens is expected to remain below eight degrees Celsius.
In Thessaloniki, cloudy conditions are forecast, with intermittent rain and isolated thunderstorms. Northwestern winds of three to four Beaufort are expected in the Thermaikos Gulf, while temperatures will range from nine to 15 degrees Celsius.
Flooding, damage in western Greece
The fire brigade has received 150 calls, carried out at least 10 water-pumping operations and evacuated three elderly residents from their homes.
In Igoumenitsa, homes and businesses have been flooded, prompting the municipal authorities to request that the municipality be declared in a state of emergency.
In Messolonghi, a 112 emergency alert was sent to residents on Friday afternoon, urging them to restrict travel to essential journeys. Flooding was reported in Messolonghi, Lesini and Aitoliko, while seven firefighters rescued two men trapped in a car in Neochori, near Messolonghi.
Southern Corfu has recorded rainfall exceeding 190 millimeters, attributed to a phenomenon known as a “fed chimney.” Rainfall totals reached 197.6 millimeters in Chlomos and 192.8 millimeters in Perivoli, while Grika in Thesprotia recorded 141.99 millimeters.

title: Nicky Henderson's Old Park Star plan for Cheltenham Festival puts bookies on 'red alert' - AOL.co.uk

full_text:
Bookmakers are on 'red alert' after Nicky Henderson suggested he would reroute one of his top horses Old Park Star.
The determined 2026 Sky Bet Supreme Novices' Hurdle winner had been the early favourite for the Arkle Chase over fences at next year's Cheltenham Festival.
However a disappointing run at Ffos Las on November 18, where Old Park Star weakened quickly in the straight under Nico de Boinville, have put those plans on hold.
It was found the Gordon and Su Hall-owned horse had bled and with time to get over that, Henderson said his charge might not have the chance to gain enough experience over the bigger obstacles.
In response to his comments, William Hill said the bookies are on 'red alert' and they expect punters to take the 16-1 for the Unibet Champion Hurdle.

"We sort of knew at the beginning of the season that we just didn’t have a Champion Hurdle horse. I say that, there’s just a chance we’re going to throw things around a bit," Henderson said on ITV's Opening Show programme.
"We might just sort of take one out of the pack that could. I’m actually talking about Old Park Star. He’s got to have a little bit of time off after his episode at Ffos Las.
"It’s possible he could, rather than have a novice chase and then he’d lose his novice chase status and then he’d only have one run before the Arkle.
"When he won his Supreme last season he was four seconds faster than the Champion Hurdle, so he must go around there quite quickly. It’s a very open Champion Hurdle."
Several firms have already cut the price of Old Park Star to 12-1, with reigning heroine of the two-mile championship race Lossiemouth the evens favourite and Mydaddypaddy is the only horse behind her in single figures (7-1).
William Hill spokesman Lee Phelps said: “Old Park Star is 16-1 for the Champion Hurdle, a price we felt was fair given there was always a chance he could switch back to hurdles if his chasing campaign didn't go to plan.
“However, Nicky Henderson appears to have suggested on this morning's Opening Show that a return to hurdles is now likely, so we'd expect that 16-1 to prove popular with punters.
“With few credible challengers to Lossiemouth at present, Old Park Star could be an interesting Champion Hurdle contender, now back in the picture.”
